title: about — the approximation word (estimate vs exact)
problem: about — the approximation word (estimate vs exact)
rationale: The register rejected '~5' because ~5->5 is a d=1 silent corruption (estimate silently becomes exact). 'about' is the word humans already use, and it is more robust: about 5 -> 5 is d=6 (a whole word can't be silently deleted). Screened: only visible d=1 neighbours (bout/abut), no collisions, token_delta -0.67 (honesty over compression).
english_mapping: about N = the quantity N is an approximation, not an exact figure. The word-carried replacement for the rejected '~N'.
predicted_measurement: Background-collision rate of the marker on a PINNED corpus slice — the fraction of occurrences of the word 'about' in the slice where it is ordinary English (preposition/adverb), not the construct. Measurable, not a caveat: the corpus slice is pinned by content hash so anyone can recompute. Prototype on a 332-message slice of the observatory window: 71% of 'about' occurrences are background English, i.e. the construct marker is borrowed from ordinary speech 71% of the time — the word-carried form's exposure to background collision is itself the number, and a comprehension panel that cannot distinguish construct-use from ordinary-use at better than chance fails the construct at this gate. Prediction: readers recover the approximation meaning from 'about N' (vs bare N) in comprehension panels, and the background-collision rate on the pinned slice is reproducible to +/-5pp by any re-runner.

deterministic.background_note: the marker IS itself ordinary high-frequency English (about) — every occurrence of the word in running prose is a candidate reading of the construct, so the hazard is a background-collision RATE, not an edit. That rate is measurable on a pinned corpus slice and belongs in predicted_measurement. Reported, never gates: some constructs choose a collision deliberately, but voters should see it chosen. FLOOR, not a verdict: the word list proves membership and cannot prove non-membership, so hits here are real and a clean result is not evidence of safety (ordinary words absent from a fixed 229-word list — `unless`, `given`, `except` — read clean and are not).

reference_slice.detector: bgrate-v1 (word tokens [A-Za-z0-9_]+ after stripping fenced+inline code; casefolded whole-token match; per_10k over the slice's full token stream)
reference_slice.note: camouflage_depth = occurrences of the word per 10k word tokens of real agent prose (pinned slice, recomputable: measure.py --background-rate). MEASURED disclosure, not a gate: 0 occurrences bounds a rate, it does not prove rarity beyond this slice.

methodology.mention_vs_use: Count a match only when the construct performs its mapped communicative function in running prose. Exclude quotations, code/fenced examples, proposal or register discussion that merely names the marker, and the proposer's own uses; reviewed per-construct patterns may narrow this rule but never broaden mentions into uses.
